questions.lead: Kimi Antonelli won Sunday's Italian Grand Prix at Monza, the first Italian driver to win his home race since 1966. He started from nineteenth on the grid.
questions.prompt: Which team was he driving for?

questions.lead: On Tuesday, mathematicians at OpenAI announced that thousands of autonomous AI agents had resolved one of the six remaining Millennium Prize problems, a question about the equations of fluid flow. The result was formally checked in the Lean proof language.
questions.prompt: Which problem did they claim to have settled?

questions.lead: A homeowner in Rebild, Denmark, digging to lay a terrace, uncovered the largest hoard of Viking silver ever found in the country: bracelets, coins, silver bars and a small Thor's hammer, roughly 700 pieces in all.
questions.prompt: How much does the hoard weigh?

questions.lead: Saturn's north pole has been ringed by a six-sided cloud, a hexagon, since Voyager data revealed it in 1987. This week NASA's Astronomy Picture of the Day showed Hubble's view of a matching geometric pattern at the south pole.
questions.prompt: How many sides does the southern pattern have?

questions.lead: Most of the Rebild hoard's roughly 700 pieces were scattered through the soil, but one group of objects was found together inside a single pottery vessel.
questions.prompt: About how many objects were in the vessel?

explanations: Antonelli was driving for Mercedes, and his team-mate George Russell finished second, 3.857 seconds behind. Max Verstappen completed the podium for Red Bull.

The claim concerns the Navier-Stokes equations, which use Newton's second law of motion to describe how fluids, from ocean currents to air flows, behave. Each of the six remaining Millennium Prize problems carries a $1 million prize from the Clay Mathematics Institute.
The hoard weighs more than 40 pounds and holds roughly 700 artefacts. Denmark's second-largest collection of Viking silver, Terslevskat, weighs 14.5 pounds.

Hubble observations show a ten-sided pattern, a decagon, around Saturn's south pole. The northern hexagon has proven stable for over 40 years, and how long the decagon lasts is now a question for researchers.
About 320 objects were found inside a pottery vessel, with the others scattered nearby. Experts think the treasure was buried in the tenth century.

sources.excerpt: The 2026 Italian Grand Prix was held on 6 September 2026 at the Monza Circuit in Monza, Italy. Kimi Antonelli (Mercedes) won from nineteenth position on the grid. Antonelli became the first Italian driver since Ludovico Scarfiotti in 1966 to win the Italian Grand Prix. Russell finished 3.857 seconds behind the winner.

mathematicians at OpenAI announced that a group of 10,000 autonomous AI agents under their direction, running on an advanced model not available to the public, had found a 'singularity' in the Navier-Stokes equations in three dimensions. Their result has been formally checked in the programming language Lean, giving mathematicians confidence that it is indeed correct. one of the six remaining Millennium Prize Problems posed in 2000 by the Clay Mathematics Institute, each of which carries a $1 million prize

The treasure includes roughly 700 artifacts and weighs more than 40 pounds. About 320 objects were found inside a pottery vessel, while the others were scattered nearby. Experts think these items were buried in the tenth century. The Rebild hoard easily surpasses Denmark's second-largest collection of Viking silver, a 14.5-pound assortment called Terslevskat.

Saturn's North Pole has been known to be surrounded by a hexagonal (6 sides) cloud since discovery in 1987 in data taken by NASA's Voyager spacecrafts, which quickly flew past the ringed world in the early 1980s. Now, recent observations of Saturn by the Hubble Space Telescope reveal a slightly different geometric cloud pattern around the South Pole: a decagon (10 sides). The northern hexagon has proven stable for over 40 years.
